newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Supreme Court denies with finality the move of PIRMA which wanted to change the Constitions and give President Fidel Ramos a chance to seek a reelection next year (ALL PAPERS)
- Executive Secretary Ruben Torres says a Charter change can still be done through a constituent assembly or a constitutional convention (TODAY)
- Singaporean Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says the restoration of Philippine-Singapore relations will not be threatened again. (MANILA TIMES)
- Immigration commissioner Edgar Mendoza suspends two officers who approved the departure of two Filipinos with tampered passports. (PHILIPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- A lower court has put a temporary freeze on the implementation of a government programme allowing the entry of more agricultural products at lower tariff rates. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Some bank-creditors of the beleagurered Victorias Milling Corp are pushing for a separate restructuring arragement for the parent firm and its subsidiaries (PHILIPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Passenger car sales continue to slacken reaching only 33,912 units as of May from 35,995 in the same period last year. (BUSINESS DAILY)
